headline: The Plumber Foundation
threshold: By Lesson 10, you can greet a customer, give times and measurements, describe pipes and fixtures, ask simple questions and make polite requests on the job, and start Plumber Lesson 1.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Pronounce common plumbing words and greet a customer or coworker politely at the job.
lessons.focus: The five vowels, ch, j, ll, rr, ñ and the written accent, in greetings and plumbing words

words.note: Feminine noun that takes el before the stressed a: el agua fría.
ll sounds like English y: YAH-veh. In Mexico it also means wrench or key.
ñ sounds like ny in canyon: BAH-nyo.
ch as in church; rr is a strong rolled r.
j sounds like a strong English h: HOON-tah.
The accent marks the stress: tu-be-RÍ-a.
A woman is la plomera.
A woman is la ayudante.
A single r between vowels is a quick tap, like dd in ladder.
b and v sound the same in Spanish.

words.en: Nice to meet you, my name is Ana.

words.note: Formal: use with customers and building managers.

lessons.speaking: Greet a homeowner at the door, say your name, say you are the plumber, and ask how they are.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Say numbers, start times and pipe measurements in feet, inches and gallons on a plumbing job.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time with a las, and feet, inches, gallons and pounds with de

words.note: Plural los pies: 10 pies de tubo.
Use a las for the time something happens.

words.es: Son 10 pies de tubo de cobre.
El tubo es de 3/4 de pulgada.
words.note: Say tres cuartos de pulgada.

lessons.speaking: Tell your helper what time you start, how many feet of pipe you need, and how big the pipe is.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Say what a pipe is made of and describe whether valves and drains are open, closed or broken.
lessons.focus: ser for what something is or is made of, estar for its condition or location

words.note: Agrees with the noun: la llave está cerrada.

words.es: La llave de paso está cerrada.
words.note: estar: a condition that can change.
ser + de for what something is made of.

words.en: The water heater is in the basement.
words.es: El calentador está en el sótano.
words.note: estar for location.
ser for jobs, with no article. A man says Soy plomero.

lessons.speaking: Describe a bathroom to your helper: say what the pipe is made of, where the valve is, and if it is open, closed or broken.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what tools you have and need, report a leak, and say what must be done first.
lessons.focus: tener, hay, necesitar, querer and hay que + infinitive

words.note: For PVC, people say pegamento para PVC.
Common job word in Mexico and the US for any pipe wrench.
Mexico and the US; balde in other countries.

words.en: There's a leak under the kitchen sink.
words.es: Hay una fuga debajo del fregadero.

words.note: Formal usted, for a customer.

words.en: We have to shut off the water first.
words.es: Hay que cerrar el agua primero.
words.note: hay que + infinitive: it's necessary to do something.

words.en: The customer wants a new faucet.
words.es: La clienta quiere una llave nueva.

words.en: I have the gloves in the truck.
words.es: Tengo los guantes en la troca.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker what you have in the truck, what tool you need, and what you have to do first on the job.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Say where you are going, what you are going to do today, and ask if you can enter a room.
lessons.focus: ir, ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer, and poder

words.note: Common US Spanish loanword on job sites; camioneta is also used.
Mexican Spanish; it can also mean in a little while.

words.en: I'm going to the store for elbows.
words.es: Voy a la tienda por codos.

words.en: We're going to replace the pipe today.
words.es: Vamos a cambiar el tubo hoy.
words.note: ir a + infinitive for plans.

words.en: I'm going to make a hole in the wall.
words.es: Voy a hacer un agujero en la pared.

words.en: May I go into the kitchen?
words.note: Polite way to ask a customer before entering a room.

words.en: I'm doing the pressure test right now.
words.es: Hago la prueba de presión ahorita.

words.en: My helper is going to the truck.
words.es: Mi ayudante va a la troca.

lessons.speaking: Tell your helper where you are going and what you are going to do today, and ask a customer if you can go into the kitchen.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Describe daily plumbing work with present tense verbs for yourself, the customer and the crew.
lessons.focus: Present tense of regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs for yo, tú, usted, nosotros and ellos

words.note: Also called el baño or la taza in Mexico.
Mexico and the US; ducha in other countries.
The ü is pronounced: des-A-gweh.
A woman is la clienta.

words.en: They sell hoses at the store.
words.es: Ellos venden mangueras en la tienda.

words.note: Informal tú, between coworkers.

lessons.speaking: Tell a customer what you are checking, what drips, and until what time your crew works today.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask a homeowner or supplier simple questions about leaks, valves, prices and fixtures.
lessons.focus: Question words qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué and cuál, with rising intonation

words.note: ¿cuántos? for how many: ¿Cuántos codos?
Two words in a question; porque (one word) means because.
A woman is la dueña.

words.en: Since when has it been dripping?

words.es: ¿Quién es el dueño de la casa?

lessons.speaking: Ask a homeowner where the shutoff valve is, which faucet drips, and since when it has been dripping.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Say what is missing or not done yet, and ask for more, less or another part on the job.
lessons.focus: no, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, and comparing with más, menos and otro

words.note: After a verb it needs no: No toco nada.
Never say un otro: otro codo, otra llave.

words.en: We don't touch anything before shutting off the water.
words.es: No tocamos nada antes de cerrar el agua.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker there is no hot water yet, nobody uses this bathroom, and you need another elbow.

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Politely ask a customer to open doors, move things and wait while you work.
lessons.focus: ¿Puede + infinitive? and usted commands for everyday verbs, with por favor

words.note: Say it when you pass by someone or enter a room.
Also means the entrance.

words.en: Can you open the door, please?
Can you move your car, please?
Please take the things out of the cabinet.
words.es: Saque las cosas del gabinete, por favor.
words.note: Usted command: sacar becomes saque.

words.es: No use el baño, por favor.

lessons.speaking: Politely ask a customer to open the door, move the car, and take the things out of the cabinet before you start.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Recognize plumbing cognates and use survival phrases to get help when you don't understand.
lessons.focus: Cognates ending in -ción, -dad and -ente, and survival phrases for getting help

words.note: -ción words are feminine: la reparación, la instalación.
-dad words are feminine.

words.en: How do you say "wrench" in Spanish?
I don't understand. Can you repeat?
It's an emergency, I need help.
One moment, I shut off the water and call my supervisor.
words.es: Un momento, cierro el agua y llamo a mi supervisor.
words.note: Use the personal a before a person: llamo a mi supervisor.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker it is an emergency, say you don't understand, and ask how to say a tool in Spanish.
